events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.entity.living.LivingDeathEvent (NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.register(this) in onInitialize, @SubscribeEvent(priority = EventPriority.NORMAL) — NORMAL and receiveCanceled=false are both the annotation defaults, so cancelled deaths are skipped)
notes:
SOURCE FOOTPRINT: the whole module is ONE file, src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/death_coordinates/DeathCoordinatesModule.java (142 lines). No config subclass (it passes AbstractModuleConfig::createDefault, i.e. DefaultModuleConfig, which adds nothing beyond enabled/debug_logging), no mixin package (grep for "death" in vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json and in mixin/ returns nothing), no commands, no items/blocks/entities (no DeferredRegister anywhere), no assets beyond lang entries, no dataGlobs in build.gradle, the module page is docs/modules/death_coordinates.md.

NO MOD GATE: no shouldInitialize() override, no ModList.isLoaded() anywhere in the module — so neither required nor optional mods. AbstractModule.shouldInitialize() defaults to true (core/AbstractModule.java:112-114).

CONFIG: only the two standard keys from AbstractModuleConfig.buildConfig — `enabled` (default = module.isEnabledByDefault(), and the module does NOT override the Module interface default `true`, core/Module.java:73-75) and `debug_logging` (enum AUTO/ON/OFF, default AUTO). Proof in the generated config test-server/config/vanillaplusadditions-common.toml:179-184. buildModuleSpecificConfig is never overridden, so configKeys is genuinely empty.

README CONTRADICTION (important for the doc writer): README.md:189 says "operators can click the message to teleport to the death location". The code checks `player.hasPermissions(2)` on the DYING player (line 107), not on the recipient. The hover+click event is baked into the single `deathMessage` component, which is then broadcast unchanged to EVERY online player (lines 128-131). Consequence: if an op dies, everyone gets a clickable message — and a non-op who clicks it just gets the command rejected, because the click runs `/execute in <dim> as @s run tp @s x y z` with the clicker's own permissions. Conversely, if a normal player dies, not even an op gets a clickable message. The README wording implies a per-recipient check that does not exist.

DEAD LANG KEYS: `message.vpa.death_coords` and `message.vpa.death_coords.hover` exist in ALL SIX lang files (en_us.json:178-179, de_de.json:178-179, de_at.json:21-22, cs_cz.json:21-22, es_es.json:21-22, fr_fr.json:21-22) but are referenced NOWHERE in src/ (grep "death_coords" over src/ hits only those lang files). The module builds every string with Component.literal in hardcoded English. History explains it: CHANGELOG 0.10.3 ("Code-Bereinigung: Hardcoded Strings in `MobGlowModule` und `DeathCoordinatesModule` wurden durch translatable Components ersetzt", CHANGELOG.md:1312) moved the strings to translatable Components, and CHANGELOG 0.12.0 ("DeathCoordinatesModule und MobGlowModule: Spieler-/Command-Feedback auf direkte Textausgaben umgestellt", CHANGELOG.md:1297) moved them back to literals — the translations were left behind. (There is no 0.11.2 release in CHANGELOG.md at all; the version numbers around this go 0.10.3 → 0.11.0 → 0.11.1 → 0.12.0.) So the chat message is English-only regardless of client language, and those 12 lang entries are dead weight.

DIMENSION NAMES ARE THE ONE TRANSLATABLE PART: dimensionName() (lines 61-76) uses Component.translatableWithFallback("dimension.<namespace>.<path>", fallback) with hardcoded fallbacks "the Overworld" / "the Nether" / "the End" and the raw id for anything else. A dimension mod that ships that key gets a localized name for free; anything else shows e.g. `othermod:mining`. The javadoc explains why (1.21.1 ships no dimension.* keys at all). The CLICK EVENT deliberately keeps the raw id, because that is what `/execute in` needs (comment at lines 58-59).

TODO IN SOURCE (lines 105-106): "TODO: Make the permission level configurable aka make it a config option to enable for spectators (and/or ops) or all players". So the hardcoded level-2 gate is a known open point, not a settled design decision.

DEBUG LOGGING INCONSISTENCY: the per-death log inside `if (getConfig().shouldDebugLog())` calls getLogger().info(...) (line 134), not .debug(). Turning on debug_logging therefore writes an INFO line per player death. onCommonSetup (line 43) does use .debug() correctly. Separately, onInitialize (line 37) logs an unconditional INFO line at startup, regardless of debug_logging.

DOES NOT TOUCH VANILLA'S DEATH MESSAGE: nothing here modifies or suppresses the vanilla death message, and nothing reads the gamerule showDeathMessages. This is a SECOND, separate broadcast, so players normally see two lines per death — and the coordinate line still appears when showDeathMessages is off.

NO ENTITY FILTER BEYOND `instanceof Player`: any Player subclass dying triggers the announcement, including fake players from other mods — there is no UUID/fake-player check.

CONSOLE COPY: after broadcasting, the same component goes to the server console via server.sendSystemMessage (line 139).

`Objects.requireNonNull(level.getServer())` (line 128) would NPE on a level without a server; in practice unreachable after the isClientSide() early return.

CANCELLED DEATHS ARE SKIPPED: LivingDeathEvent implements ICancellableEvent (verified in the NeoForge sources jar), and @SubscribeEvent.receiveCanceled defaults to false (verified with javap on bus-8.0.5's SubscribeEvent.class: AnnotationDefault Z#14 = false). So if another mod cancels the death (totem-style saves) nothing is announced. Correct behaviour, but worth stating since it is implicit. The explicit `priority = EventPriority.NORMAL` is likewise the annotation default — it changes nothing.

HISTORICAL FIX WORTH MENTIONING: CHANGELOG 0.13.4 (CHANGELOG.md:1256-1258) fixed the teleport command from `@p` to `@s` — before that, clicking teleported an arbitrary nearby player instead of the clicker. The inline comment at line 116 documents this.

STANDALONE JAR: build.gradle:419 lists `[ moduleId: 'death_coordinates', displayName: 'Vanilla Plus: Death Coordinates' ]` with no mixins, no dataGlobs and no moduleDeps — so the standalone jar is just vpa_core + this one class. Entrypoint: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/standalone/death_coordinates/DeathCoordinatesStandalone.java, @Mod("vpa_death_coordinates").

BUNDLE REGISTRATION: VanillaPlusAdditions.java:160, `moduleManager.registerModule(new DeathCoordinatesModule());` (import at line 13). The only other file in src/ that references the module is the standalone entrypoint named above.
oneLiner: When any player dies, everyone on the server gets a chat line naming the player, the exact X/Y/Z of the death and the dimension — and if the player who died was an operator, that line is clickable and teleports whoever clicks it to the spot, provided they themselves may run commands.
shortDescription: Announces the coordinates of player deaths in chat
